assessment.nobel_worthiness: Foundational, long-lived contributions to the political economy of trade policy ('Protection for Sale') and, with the same pair, to the integration of innovation and endogenous growth with international trade. The framework shaped both theory and empirical work on trade policy and interest-group influence.
assessment.attribution: The credit is concentrated in a clear, long-standing two-person partnership, so the proposed pair is clean. Related contributors such as Krugman (already recognised in 2008) and Melitz sit in adjacent lines and do not weaken the pair's claim.
assessment.maturity: Core work dates from the 1990s and is thoroughly tested, taught and extended. The timing risk is age and the fact that trade has already been recognised, not insufficient confirmation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee reads the political-economy-of-protection work as a distinct enough advance from the 2008 trade prize.
Whether growth-and-trade and protection-for-sale are better treated as separate prize cases.
Empirical support for the protection-for-sale model is mixed and judged differently across subfields.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework (staggered pricing, interest-rate rules, the microfounded policy-analysis apparatus) is the workhorse of modern monetary policy analysis and central-bank practice. Its impact on how policy is designed and communicated is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts) and Woodford (the unified theory of monetary policy) are the clearest foundational credits. Gali, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum, Smets and others contributed significantly through estimation and DSGE, and the three-name limit forces hard exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in policy institutions give strong confirmation. Performance around the 2008 crisis and the post-pandemic inflation episode drew critiques but also further development.
uncertainties: How to divide credit among the many significant contributors, including those excluded by the three-name limit.
Some of the monetary-policy territory is adjacent to the 2022 prize and to earlier recognitions of rational-expectations macro.
Critiques of DSGE models after 2008 and 2021-22 could temper enthusiasm.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore model of credit cycles showed how collateral constraints propagate and amplify shocks, a central mechanism in macro-finance. It underlies much post-2008 work on financial frictions and macroprudential policy.
assessment.attribution: The collateral-constraint credit-cycle mechanism has a crisp two-author origin. Gertler, Gilchrist and Bernanke are central to the related financial-accelerator line, and Bernanke is already a laureate (2022), which makes a Gertler-Gilchrist pairing a weaker alternative.
assessment.maturity: The 1997 paper has had nearly three decades of development and confirmation, and the financial crisis raised its empirical relevance.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on banking, crises and financial frictions may count against it.
Whether the committee would prefer to include Gertler for the financial-accelerator side.
Quantitative empirical identification of these mechanisms is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The alternating-offers bargaining model with a unique subgame-perfect equilibrium became the standard non-cooperative treatment of bargaining. It spawned a large literature on bargaining and search in markets and is used throughout theory and applied fields.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein (1982) is the unambiguous core. Wolinsky's contribution (decentralised trade and bargaining in markets, with Rubinstein) is a clear extension. Binmore's contribution is significant but more of a complement, and Stahl's earlier related work is not on the list.
assessment.maturity: More than four decades of theory and applications. Mature, but game theory has had several recent prizes (2005, 2007, 2012, 2020).
uncertainties: Possible reluctance to give another game-theory prize soon after earlier ones.
Whether Wolinsky's share is sufficient to merit inclusion, versus Rubinstein alone.
Overlap with search-and-matching recognition (Diamond, Mortensen, Pissarides, 2010).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical work on technological change, tasks and the China trade shock reshaped understanding of labour-market adjustment, local labour-market effects and policy debates. The influence on economics and on public discussion is very broad.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the common thread across the task-based and trade-shock work. Dorn and Hanson are strong co-authors on the China-shock papers. Katz and Levy-Murnane / Acemoglu-Restrepo contributions to the task framework are partly outside this ballot.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock papers date from about 2013 onward and are well cited, but there is ongoing debate on magnitudes, persistence and identification.
uncertainties: Debate on the size and persistence of the trade-shock effects.
Theory of tasks is shared with others not credited here, which complicates the attribution of the conceptual framework.
Recent enough that further evidence may refine the conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that misallocation of resources across firms can account for a large share of cross-country income and TFP differences, an influential bridge between micro data and macro development and growth. It is widely used in development and growth accounting.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) are the central empirical-quantitative authors. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) developed a closely related framework, and Rogerson is not on this ballot, so the attribution is incomplete and contested.
assessment.maturity: About 15 years of use. Its measurement approach has been debated, notably on measurement error in the dispersion of marginal products.
uncertainties: Priority between Hsieh-Klenow and Restuccia-Rogerson, and omission of Rogerson from the list.
Sensitivity of results to measurement error and to modelling assumptions.
Still relatively recent compared with the longest-established candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Obstfeld-Rogoff's intertemporal open-economy approach (the 'redux' model) and their exchange-rate disconnect and puzzles work set the framework for modern international macroeconomics. Influential textbook and policy applications.
assessment.attribution: The two-person attribution is reasonably clean for the core framework. Other contributors (Dornbusch, Lane, Gourinchas and Rey, Engel and others) are outside the proposed pair.
assessment.maturity: Mature work from the 1990s with extensive use, though the empirical puzzles remain largely unresolved.
uncertainties: The disconnect puzzles remain unresolved, which may be read as unfinished science.
Rogoff's other work (B028) is a separate and contested line.
Dornbusch's early overshooting contributions complicate the story of origins.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The exhaustible-resources theory (Dasgupta-Heal) and later work on natural capital, biodiversity and inclusive wealth form an important part of the foundations of resource and environmental economics, with continuing relevance for sustainability measurement.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal share the foundational resource-economics credit. Solow, Stiglitz and Hotelling lines are adjacent and partly overlap, with Solow and Nordhaus (2018) already recognised.
assessment.maturity: Core results date from the 1970s and are mature. Later inclusive-wealth and biodiversity work is more policy-oriented and less settled as science.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of Solow and Nordhaus in growth and environment.
Difference between foundational theory and the later, less consolidated, policy-oriented work.
Candidate age and how much weight inclusive-wealth measurement deserves.
